source.scope: All 17 printed CCPh ASOP steps and identified supplemental in-volume families. Campaign/module/equipment profiles need their own reconciliation.

scope: Cross-phase dependency design for the completed ASL.Rules implementation. All identified pending procedures stay visible. This is not an executable rules scheduler or a certification of every SSR/module.

chains.title: CX survives the turn, but has several release events
chains.origin: Double Time, difficult advance or another rule gives a unit CX.
chains.due: Breaking, or the applicable event in its next friendly Player Turn under A4.51; not ordinary end-CCPh cleanup.
checks: Keep the unit and creation turn. CX still affects intervening attacks, Ambush, CC, Recovery and difficult advance.

In its next Player Turn, remove at the first applicable event: completion of all Prep Fire, Opportunity Fire designation, movement, becoming TI, or conclusion of its MPh. Apply A4.51’s start-of-MPh removal and retain the prohibition on Double Time that MPh.
Do not remove CX before its final Prep Fire attack. Preserve prior-CX history after removing the counter, and distinguish new CX caused by Minimum Move or Deep Stream Entry.
chains.example: A squad made CX in APh stays CX through CC and the opposing turn; removing its old CX in its next MPh does not let it Double Time again.
chains.status: Execution coverage is mixed; verify the full linked rule path. Pending rules remain visible.

chains.title: DM cleanup follows Rally attempts
chains.origin: Breaking and specified subsequent attack, adjacency or Rout-start conditions create DM.
chains.due: End of each RPh, after Rally attempts, with voluntary-retention and continuing conditions.
checks: Carry DM into the Rally roll; do not clear it on opening Rally.
Retain the legal terrain/overstacking choice and re-evaluate the conditions that impose DM. Rout permission and compulsory rout are separate findings.
A later qualifying attack or Known-enemy condition can impose DM again; a previous cleanup does not immunize the unit.
chains.example: A broken unit cannot improve its current Rally attempt by clearing DM early, but may legally retain DM to preserve a later rout option.
chains.status: Execution coverage is mixed; verify the full linked rule path. Pending rules remain visible.

chains.title: Shock and UK use the next Rally, not Stun cleanup
chains.origin: A vehicle receives Shock or has an existing UK counter returned to Shock.
chains.due: End of the next RPh; UK then has its own next-RPh recuperation test.
checks: Record the next eligible RPh and the current Shock/UK state. It is not restricted to the owner’s Rally.
Shock recuperates on 1-2, otherwise becomes UK; UK recuperates on 1-3, otherwise wrecks without Crew Survival. A new Shock result can reset UK to Shock.
Do not erase the vehicle’s earlier movement history when Shock halts it. No Stun flip or generic end-turn removal substitutes for recuperation.
chains.example: A shocked moving tank stops immediately, retains applicable moving-target history, and waits for the next Rally recuperation window.
chains.status: Execution coverage is mixed; verify the full linked rule path. Pending rules remain visible.

chains.title: Stun flips once and preserves its lasting penalty
chains.origin: An eligible crew suffers Stun or Recall.
chains.due: Normal Stun flips at the end of that Player Turn, ASOP 8.43B; Recall and cumulative exceptions remain separate.
checks: Keep the persistent +1 and the identity of the affected crew, including when it abandons and later re-crews a vehicle.
Do not restore CE as a side effect of flipping Stun. Apply D5.33 in a subsequent Player Turn.
An incoming-RPh reminder must not execute the same boundary transition twice. Shock, Recall and LC/LVT exceptions use their own rules.
chains.example: The next Rally sees a +1 marker, not a fresh Stun recovery roll or automatic restoration of CE.
chains.status: Execution coverage is mixed; verify the full linked rule path. Pending rules remain visible.

chains.title: Pin and ordinary TI survive until after combat and work
chains.origin: A unit is pinned or becomes TI; a terrain or vehicle procedure uses a Pin marker for a different purpose.
chains.due: Ordinary Pin/TI removal at 8.43B, after Location combat and Clearance; earlier break and special-duration rules still apply.
checks: Pinned/TI units do not regain APh or CC capabilities retroactively when the counter is removed.
Breaking removes ordinary TI under A4.8, but must also invalidate any work whose eligibility has been lost.
Keep Animal-Pack, replenishment and LC-Blaze Pin durations separate. A counter’s printed label alone is not its expiry rule.
chains.example: A pinned squad cannot advance merely because Pin will disappear later in the same Player Turn.
chains.status: Execution coverage is mixed; verify the full linked rule path. Pending rules remain visible.

chains.title: MPh fire commitments survive into DFPh
chains.origin: A defender fires during an expenditure, leaving unit/weapon fire states and possibly residual.
chains.due: Remove residual at MPh end; carry fire eligibility into DFPh; ordinary First/Final counters leave at daytime DFPh end or night AFPh end.
checks: Keep per-unit and per-weapon use, ROF and CA/direction commitments after each shot.
Residual expiry does not restore a First-Fired or Final-Fired subject. A pass on one expenditure does not finish all defensive opportunities.
At night retain the original Gunflash Location even when the firing unit moves away.
chains.example: The Fire Lane disappears at MPh end, while the MG’s earlier fire still governs its DFPh choices.
chains.status: Execution coverage is mixed; verify the full linked rule path. Pending rules remain visible.

chains.title: Opportunity Fire needs a preserved reservation
chains.origin: Eligible Infantry/Cavalry declares Opportunity Fire in PFPh.
chains.due: Use the reservation in AFPh, then remove its Bounding Fire marker at 5.33B.
checks: Preserve the reason for the Bounding Fire counter: an Opportunity Firer is an explicit AFPh exception, not an ordinary spent firer.
Prevent MPh movement and impermissible CA changes. Recheck actual AFPh eligibility without erasing the earlier commitment.
Keep eligible ROF/IF and weapon/Spotter restrictions. Considered does not reserve or release a shot.
chains.example: A reserved mortar can use its special AFPh opportunity only through the preserved Spotter and firing conditions.

chains.title: A vehicle carryover shot depends on the whole MPh
chains.origin: A vehicle ends its MPh with retained Multiple ROF on a weapon.
chains.due: At most the specific D3.32 shot in its AFPh, if no other weapon including PRC fired in its MPh.
checks: Retain all vehicle and PRC firing history, not just the selected weapon’s ROF.
This is not ordinary Opportunity Fire or a full new ROF sequence; apply its one-shot limit and appropriate Motion/non-Motion treatment.
Marker cleanup later cannot retroactively make the carryover legal.
chains.example: An MA with retained ROF loses this opportunity if another weapon or PRC fired during that MPh.

chains.title: Stopping and removing markers do not erase movement
chains.origin: A target moves, uses VBM, is in Motion, or a weapon/operator changes position.
chains.due: Keep the history for the rule’s Player-Turn scope; re-evaluate the narrower expenditure modifiers at each phase boundary.
checks: Do not apply MPh FFNAM/FFMO or J1/J2 as though DFPh were another expenditure response.
Preserve qualifying Case J vehicle history after a Stop or Shock. Hazardous Movement has its own activity duration.
Keep operator movement and weapon movement distinct for later AFPh eligibility.
chains.example: A stopped tank can still be a moving target in DFPh even though Infantry FFNAM no longer applies.

chains.due: Resolve the Placed DC in AFPh 5.22A, with the placement record’s applicable conditions.
checks: Record placement success, target and relevant approach/attack facts before moving to another expenditure.
Do not offer a second ordinary firing eligibility check as a substitute for resolving an operably Placed DC.
Set DC and Thrown DC have different triggers and persistence; do not schedule every DC for AFPh automatically.
chains.example: The carrier becoming ineligible for ordinary AFPh fire does not erase an already operably Placed DC.

chains.title: Non-Flame Clearance resolves after CC, not on declaration
chains.origin: An eligible MPh/DFPh declaration identifies participants, task and target; Flail has its own MPh declaration.
chains.due: Resolve the eligible non-Flame task at 8.42B before ordinary Pin/TI cleanup.
checks: Retain declaration and participation history, the exact task, its target/hexside, Labor and partial work.
Loss of eligibility does not become harmless because TI or Pin is about to be removed. Recheck the task’s conditions before rolling.
Do not open every task in DFPh: its printed list differs from MPh. Named O1.5/module profiles remain source-gated.
chains.example: A Wire attempt declared in DFPh is still pending while the player resolves every CC Location.

chains.title: New and Hampered Flames need distinct origins
chains.origin: A Flame is created, or an immediate MPh/DFPh Flame Clearance attempt Hampers it.
chains.due: Exclude new/Hampered Flames from that Player Turn’s conversion; clear the appropriate Pin at CCPh cleanup.
checks: Resolve Flame Clearance immediately. It does not wait with the non-Flame tasks until CCPh.
A Final Fire Clearance DR of 3-6 Hampers the Flame for that Player Turn; store that cause separately from new-Flame age.
Build the Blaze-spread queue before the Flame-conversion queue. A newly created Flame cannot cascade into a Blaze in the same AFPh.
chains.example: An unsuccessful extinction attempt can still prevent conversion this turn; showing only success or failure loses that result.

chains.title: Blaze escape deadlines depend on the occupant
chains.origin: Terrain becomes Blaze while occupied, or a glider/parachute lands there.
chains.due: Infantry: end of next RtPh. Vehicular/Cavalry units: next friendly MPh. Landing and entry have their own immediate/end-MPh consequences.
checks: Create a subject-specific obligation when Blaze appears, not only when Rout opens.
Retain the Melee/Pin restrictions and the special escape procedure for qualifying units that cannot voluntarily break.
Do not apply the Infantry deadline to every vehicle or exempt night units from the Blaze requirement.

chains.title: Ordinary smoke ages on its owner’s Prep Fire
chains.origin: Place a typed SMOKE effect with owner, source, size and full/dispersed state.
chains.due: White Dispersed SMOKE: owner’s next PFPh opening; then disperse remaining white SMOKE. Ordinary half-inch SMOKE: MPh end, with cave exception.
checks: Do removal before dispersal, so newly dispersed counters are not removed in the same pass.
Do not use the active player as a substitute for source ownership when expiring smoke.
Keep Gusts, weather, drifting smoke, Napalm and cave smoke as distinct transition rules.
chains.example: Smoke laid by the defender is not removed just because the attacker begins Prep Fire.

chains.title: Drift depends on its source, while Gusts act twice
chains.origin: Wind/force changes, a source disperses or disappears, or the Wind Change DR creates Gusts.
chains.due: Immediate drift invalidation when source/wind changes; eligible drift at first game RPh/each AFPh; Gusts smoke effects in RPh and again AFPh.
checks: Remove dependent gray drift immediately when its source is removed or wind direction/force changes; source dispersal removes its furthest drift counter.
Record the RPh Gusts event for later AFPh smoke and fire-spread effects. Do not reroll it or treat the RPh cleanup as the only effect.
At AFPh follow 5.11 drift, 5.12 WP and 5.13 Gusts order; cave smoke uses its exceptions.
chains.example: A full-strength source becoming dispersed shortens its drift immediately, before the next routine drift placement window.
chains.status: Execution coverage is mixed; verify the full linked rule path. Pending rules remain visible.

chains.title: Night Gunflash is Location evidence, not illumination
chains.origin: A qualifying attack or another night procedure creates Gunflash evidence.
chains.due: Retain ordinary night fire markers through AFPh, then perform 5.33B cleanup; continuing Melee/FFE and switched-on searchlights follow their own sources.
checks: Keep the original First/Final Fire Location even if the firing unit leaves it.
Gunflash is not illumination. Removing a generic marker does not cancel a still-existing Melee/FFE or switched-on searchlight source.
Do not make a hidden unit Known merely because its Location can be fired upon.
chains.example: A player can fire at a vacated Gunflash Location beyond NVR without knowing who, if anyone, now occupies it.

chains.title: Concealment precedes night illumination cleanup
chains.origin: Starshells or IR illuminate a Location during the Player Turn.
chains.due: Assess ATTACKER concealment at 8.44A before 8.45B Starshell/IR removal and its Acquisition check.
checks: Keep illumination active while evaluating concealment eligibility; do not darken the map early.
Apply the specific Acquisition retention test for Blaze/Flame illumination, rather than simply keeping every currently illuminated target.
Trip Flares have a different expiry rule; Gunflash alone is not a substitute for illumination.
chains.example: A unit cannot claim concealment by using darkness that will exist only after the concealment window has closed.

The triggering expenditure is illuminated for its own consequences. Resolve activation before the appropriate response.
A later-phase flare survives the current CCPh and the next Rally/Prep/Movement/Defensive Fire windows.
chains.example: A flare triggered by a rout must remain when the player presses End Player Turn.

chains.title: Artillery has mission, contact and entry clocks
chains.origin: A battery places SR/FFE and maintains separate Contact and Access states.
chains.due: Ordinary FFE:1 becomes FFE:2 after resolution; next friendly PFPh/DFPh resolution changes FFE:2 to FFE:C. FFE:C has fire-phase and end-RPh consequences.
checks: Entering/becoming more vulnerable in an existing HE/WP Blast Area during MPh/RtPh/APh/CCPh can cause a subject-only attack; it does not advance the mission counter or attack the whole hex.
Retain the distinct end-RPh Access/Contact cleanup and next-friendly-fire-phase continuation decision. Involuntary contact loss is not automatic cancellation of every mission.
Rocket, Barrage, NOBA and illumination schedules must use their own profiles rather than the ordinary HE cycle.
chains.example: A squad entering FFE:C in Advance can be attacked even though no new artillery mission is being called.

chains.title: Acquisition persists until a defined loss event
chains.origin: A qualifying weapon acquires a unit or area.
chains.due: Track through movement, rout, advance and withdrawal; remove or transfer only on the specified weapon, operator, target or night events.
checks: Record weapon identity, target type, acquired subject/Location and observer-safe LOS history.
Movement, loss of possession/Good Order, malfunction, particular ammunition/fire choices and CA changes can invalidate Acquisition before any phase-end cleanup.
Do not erase ordinary Acquisition at every phase boundary, or treat tracking as permission to fire during Rout/Advance/CC Withdrawal.

chains.title: Ammunition replenishment counts complete Game Turns
chains.origin: Eligible Low Ammo vehicle and compatible supply commit to TI in the same/Accessible Locations.
chains.due: One, two or three complete Game Turns for B# at most 9, 10 or 11; completion at the applicable CCPh, followed by the supply depletion DR.
checks: Count both Player Turns, RPh through CCPh inclusive. Show completed Game Turns and the currently incomplete interval.

Loss of CE, expenditure of MP, firing or being attacked in CC interrupts as specified; the interrupted Game Turn does not count. Do not erase previously completed Game Turns without a rule requiring it.
Ammo Dump/offload/transfer uses its separate four-Game-Turn procedure. Ordinary TI cleanup cannot complete either task early.
chains.example: A replenishing vehicle survives one CCPh with TI still present because its required complete Game Turn is unfinished.

chains.title: Animal Packing finishes at a later Rally window
chains.origin: Place Animal-Pack at 1.13B of the initial RPh of a Game Turn.
chains.due: After the required complete Game Turns, remove it at 1.13B in the next RPh; midpoint loading/unloading and reversal have separate rules.
checks: Count from first RPh through second CCPh, double the period at night, and preserve the rule’s minimum duration.

chains.title: Berserk recovery has several distinct windows
chains.origin: A unit becomes berserk, including the separate voluntary Dare-Death procedure.
chains.due: Test the appropriate MPh no-Known-enemy condition, AFPh halved-TPBF elimination, CC elimination, or Dare-Death end-Location condition.
checks: Preserve the actual Known-enemy and elimination history required by each test; do not replace them with a generic end-turn reset.
The AFPh and CC elimination cases require the specified enemy elimination, not merely an empty Location after other units leave.
Voluntary Dare-Death status and Tank-Hunter lifetime are not ordinary berserk recovery.

chains.title: APh entry hands a combat record to CCPh
chains.origin: Advance, reinforcement or another entry creates a CC encounter with origin and concealment history.
chains.due: Resolve one Location’s full CC sequence before the next; retain qualifying Melee into later Player Turns.
checks: Carry entry history for Ambush and Street Fighting; do not reroll Ambush for ordinary reinforcement of an existing Melee.
Freeze simultaneous declarations before results; sequential attacks reopen only after immediate consequences.
